data.cultural_impact: Bhim is a prominent figure in Hindu mythology and represents strength, power, and courage. He is also known for his unwavering loyalty to his brothers and devotion towards his wife, Draupadi. The name Bhim has been commonly used in India for centuries and continues to be a popular name among Hindus.
data.spiritual_significance: Bhim is not just a symbol of physical strength but also represents inner strength and moral courage. In Hinduism, the divine quality of Bhim serves as an inspiration for individuals to work towards overcoming obstacles, remaining faithful to their duty, and staying committed to their spiritual pursuits despite challenges.

historical_references.reference: Bhim is the second of the two sons of Vidura, a wise and just sage in the Mahabharata epic. The name Bhim is derived from the Sanskrit word 'bhima', which means 'terror' or 'strong'.

Bhim is also known as Bhima Kartikeya, the elder brother of the great warrior Bhima in Hindu mythology. He was born to King Vibhishana of Lanka and his consort Tulasi, who was also a manifestation of the goddess Tulasi. Bhima Kartikeya is considered an incarnation of Lord Subrahmanya, the warrior god.
